era_setting.place: Southern California (Anaheim, Barstow, Interstate 15, Orange County) and northern Indiana (Elkhart County; venue changed to Winamac, Pulaski County); with Ford engineering and product-review interiors, and Washington, D.C. for the federal regulator
era_setting.notes: 1968-1981 ONLY, and this is the field that will save this episode. The archive shelf is overwhelmingly contemporary: a modern hatchback, an LED headlight, a flat-screen monitor, a mobile phone, a euro number plate, a modern motorway gantry or a present-day office are all out of period here, and every one of them survives every machine gate. In period: American cars of the late 1960s and 1970s with no badge visible, two-lane and early interstate highway, typewriters and carbon paper, rotary telephones, drafting boards and parallel rules, newsprint webs and hot-metal or early offset printing, filing cabinets, CRT television, US federal and county civic architecture, and Indiana farmland. Declared because EP62 greene shipped a modern ballot and a 2011 Range Rover Evoque on an EU plate through five green gates, purely because nothing machine-readable said what century or continent the film was in -- and this episode is thirteen years older than that one.

forbidden_claims: $11 would have fixed the pinto, or any sentence putting $11 and the pinto together without saying that $11 is the rollover-compliance figure for every passenger car and light truck sold in america; the appellate court's per-car figure for a package of pinto rear-impact fixes is $15.30
ford valued a human life at $200,000 (the memo attributes the figure to nhtsa twice and states that its use does not signify that ford accepts or concurs in the values)

$200,000 was the figure nhtsa used to decide whether to issue standards (schwartz retracts this at 1024: nhtsa published the datum, did not rely on it in standard-setting, and had said it was a minimum and not a maximum; ford can fairly be faulted for ignoring that explanation)

calling the grush/saunby report the pinto memo, an internal ford memo about the pinto, or ford's secret cost-benefit analysis on the pinto (it is attachment ii to a ford petition of 19 september 1973 for reconsideration of fmvss 301, and the word pinto appears nowhere in its cost-benefit table)
showing or describing the grush/saunby report as something the grimshaw jury saw or was persuaded by -- it was excluded from evidence

any pinto death toll other than nhtsa's own compiled figures, and those only in full: 38 cases, 27 fatalities of which one is reported to have resulted from impact injuries, and 24 non-fatal burn injuries, attributed to nhtsa investigation report c7-38 of may 1978 and carried with nhtsa's own fars caveats. 500 to 900, hundreds, thousands and we will never know how many are all barred
any sentence in which the jury's $125,000,000 and the remitted $3,500,000 are not both present, or in which $125 million stands alone as what ford paid
ford paid $125 million, or any statement of what ford actually paid or when, which is in no retrieved document
the gray family recovered punitive damages, or the family won $125 million (punitive damages were grimshaw's alone; the grays were barred by california's wrongful-death rule)
ford was convicted, found guilty, or held criminally liable in indiana -- ford was acquitted on all counts on 13 march 1980
the indiana criminal case concerned the grimshaw crash (different crash, different state, different victims, two years later)

the indiana jury let ford off on a technicality, or the acquittal was bought (the retrieved account is that the reckless homicide statute was enacted only in 1977 so the design could not be prosecuted, that the resulting narrowness kept ford's internal documents out, and that the prosecutor himself described a david and goliath mismatch)

naming any ford employee as culpable, criminal, or a decision-maker who chose profit over lives -- iacocca, alexander, macdonald, kennedy, grush, saunby, hromi, maclean, misch. no court found any individual liable or guilty and the elkhart grand jury deliberately charged only the corporation. roles may be stated exactly as the opinion and the report state them and no further; harley copp may be named because the court names him as the plaintiffs' testifying witness
naming, depicting identifiably or characterising robert duggar, the van driver, who was never charged

any description of richard grimshaw's injuries beyond the two sentences the opinion gives, any invented interior life, family scene or hospital scene, and any generated image, ai video, archive photograph or dramatisation depicting him, a burned child, a burned adult, a burn victim's face, skin grafts, or a person on fire
dramatising lilly gray's death, or naming or characterising her surviving family beyond the grays and carmen gray, a minor. the spelling is lilly, as the official reporter has it, not lily
depicting the deaths of judy ulrich, lynn ulrich or donna ulrich, showing the elkhart public library photograph of the crashed 1973 pinto, or showing any vehicle presented as that car

the worst car ever made, the deadliest car in american history, a rolling firebomb or a death trap asserted in the film's own voice (these may be quoted and attributed to 1977-78 press as claims made at the time)

presenting the appellate opinion as a neutral account -- the court states that it viewed all evidence in the light most favorable to the parties prevailing below and made no attempt to review the evidence on the other litigated issues
saying pinto madness won a pulitzer prize (schwartz writes it at 1017 and this pass could not confirm it from any prize-awarding body)

merging the two ford cost-saving figures: the opinion quotes exhibit 125 as a design cost savings of $10.9 million for 1974-1975 and that is the figure the film uses; schwartz describes the same april 1971 memorandum as $31.6 million across several ford models

anything after 10 september 1981 -- what ford paid, what became of richard grimshaw, ford's later fuel-system practice, later pinto litigation, the recall completion rate beyond the 53% a nhtsa official gave schwartz by telephone, or the case's later citation history

any generated image presented as the grush/saunby report, exhibit 125, a ford crash-test report, an nhtsa letter, report or recall notice, a page of the grimshaw record, the elkhart indictment, or a period newspaper front page

CUT BUDGET, checked so the contract is satisfiable (EP66 declared one that was not): at target_cut_sec 3.7 the film holds 421 cuts at the short edge, 476 at the design centre and 512 at the long edge; stills may occupy at most 32% of cuts, so still cuts are <= 134 / 152 / 163 and video cuts are >= 287 / 324 / 349. mandatory_stills 104 therefore fits inside the still-cut ceiling at BOTH edges, and distinct_video_assets 265 fits inside the video-cut budget at BOTH edges. The footage plan allocates exactly 324 video cuts across 19 registers. FOOTAGE SUPPLY measured 2026-08-11 in one ledger pass replicating stage_footage_by_title.py's own selection: 623 queries over two rounds, 14,314 clips across 19 counted register unions, 11,089 surviving an off-register and forbidden_subjects title screen -- against 265 required. A twentieth register (heat / flame / ember, union 1,021) was measured and then REFUSED, because this film never puts fire on screen; it is excluded from those totals and 0 of its clips are staged. A hit count is not a supply count: footage_review_required is true and a labelled contact sheet must be looked at by a person, with R6 and R12 looked at first, because 'crash' returns crashing waves and 'court' returns a bird's courtship display. THE EMOTIONAL CENTRE OF THIS STORY CANNOT BE SHOWN. Richard Grimshaw was 13 and may be living; Lilly Gray died of burns; the three who died in Indiana were 16, 18 and 18. There is no depiction of any of them, no burned person, no burn injury, no crash and no fire anywhere in this film. What the film shows instead is fixed, beat by beat, in the binding substitution table at EP68_pinto_FILM_BIBLE.v001.md section 3.5, and the forbidden_subjects list below is the machine half of that same decision.
